back_translation: Woe is me! For I have become like one gathering fruit at the end of the harvest, like a gleaner after the grape harvest: there is no cluster to eat, no early-ripe fig that my soul desires.
The faithful have perished from the land, and there is no upright person left among men; they all lie in wait for blood, each hunting his brother with a net.
Their hands are skilled at evil: the official demands a bribe, the judge accepts payment, and the powerful man dictates his evil desire; so they weave their schemes together.
The best of them is like a brier, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of punishment your watchmen warned of has come; now their confusion is at hand.
Do not trust a neighbor; do not rely on a friend. Guard the words of your mouth even from the woman who lies in your arms.
For the son treats the father with contempt, the daughter rises against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the members of his own household.
But as for me, I will watch for the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
O my enemy, do not rejoice over me. Though I have fallen, I will rise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
I will bear the wrath of the LORD, because I have sinned against Him, until He pleads my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me out into the light, and I will see His righteousness.
Then my enemy will see, and shame will cover her who said to me, 'Where is the LORD your God?' My eyes will look upon her; now she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
There will be a day for rebuilding your walls; in that day your boundary will be extended far.
In that day people will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the Euphrates River, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
But the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the result of their deeds.
Shepherd Your people with Your staff, the flock of Your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest amid fertile land; let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in days of old.
The LORD says: I will show them wonders, as in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might; they will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will go deaf.
They will lick the dust like a serpent, like crawling things of the earth; they will come trembling out of their strongholds; they will come in dread to the LORD our God, and they will fear You.
Who is a God like You, who forgives iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance? He does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in steadfast love.
He will have compassion on us again; He will tread our iniquities underfoot and cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
